# `kernel/navi/NaviResourceCatalog.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/navi/NaviResourceCatalog.js`

NaviResourceCatalog.js — one deterministic, searchable projection of Navi tools, Faculties, guidance recipes, task episodes, and related resources. Catalog entries are descriptions only. Search never executes a resource or grants permission, and callers must resolve live authority independently.

## Functions

### `async projectBrokerDecisionToResourceSelection(rawInput = {}, rawOptions = {})`

Convert one existing NaviModelBroker decision into the Phase 8 resource selection contract without running a second selector. The broker's selected route and candidate order are authoritative. This projection only validates, binds, and signs that already-made decision.

### `async createNaviModelRouteResourceBindings(routeConfiguration, purpose)`

Build the exact descriptor and verifier bindings for every model route in a broker candidate set. The descriptor hash intentionally shares the execution-plan route domain so the persisted selection and executable plan attest the same normalized route. No provider content or credential enters either binding.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```
